image.title: DW
image.description: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

item.title: Polls open in Taiwan's closely watched local elections
item.description: Polls have opened for local elections in Taiwan. While campaigners have stayed away from the topic of China and focused on issues like transport and childcare, Beijing has repeatedly weighed in.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Spain's Sanchez makes final appeal to voters before election
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez told people to turn out in large numbers so the country does not go "backwards." Polls suggest an end to his eight-year leftist leadership of Spain.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: US disables ship in Gulf of Oman under Iran blockade
item.description: The United States said it was continuing "to strictly enforce the blockade" of Iran's ports. Meanwhile, Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador over a strike that killed two Italian technicians.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill
item.description: Quebec's government passed Bill 21 to ban religious symbols for public servants, arguing it was necessary to protect its secularist society. Critics argue the bill weakens legal protections for fundamental rights.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany news: Lawmakers approve debt-laden 2027 budget
item.description: German lawmakers voted on a federal budget which foresees €556 billion in spending. Elsewhere, the Left Party is hosting a summit on femicide and the BSW party conference starts in Dresden. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Spanish rider Marc Marquez announces MotoGP retirement, days after clinching record 8th world title
item.description: Marc Marquez took fans and his team by surprise when announcing this weekend's race in Valencia will be his last. The 33-year-old won a record eight MotoGP titles, including his rookie and retirement seasons.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: France seeks German man in Channel migrant boat probe
item.description: A German businessman is accused of supplying equipment to smugglers organizing migrant crossings from France to the United Kingdom. However, he can't face formal charges until he is extradited to France.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit
item.description: An EU leaders summit on the bloc's seven-year budget fell apart amid divisions over how to fund Ukraine. The budget proposal also includes a 3% tax on US tech companies, in a bid for the EU to generate additional funds.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, Brussels' most anticipated new art museum, opens its doors
item.description: A major addition to Europe's cultural scene: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, the new contemporary art museum in a former Citroen factory complex, is celebrating its opening with a free, nonstop weekend program.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Serbia's Student List runs chemistry professor Radomir Saicic for president
item.description: After ousting strongman Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's student movement has now nominated academic Radomir Saicic for the upcoming presidential vote. Saicic accused the "outgoing regime" of trying to collapse the state.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong
item.description: The tiny Vallarta mud turtle was only discovered in 2018. It's critically endangered with around 300 thought to live in the wild. Almost one tenth of that number were stashed in a traveler's luggage, bound in duct tape.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Arsenic in the water: Thailand presses Myanmar over mining pollution
item.description: Thailand is seeking to tackle river pollution stemming from rare earth mines in neighboring Myanmar. The two countries held joint talks this week as a "first step towards agreeing on the evidence."
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Georgia: Police clash with Besiktas fans at Israel club game
item.description: Turkey's Besiktas accused Georgian police of using "disproportionate" force during the game with Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva, which saw Besiktas fans unfurl a banner supporting Palestine.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, succumbing to aviation fuel costs
item.description: The low-cost airline was only founded a few years ago and had been struggling to turn a profit. The spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran has now driven Norway's Norse Atlantic into bankruptcy.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: As Gambia gears up for election, can Barrow secure a third term?
item.description: President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term as Gambians vote on December 5. The election will test the opposition's appeal and the country's progress on democratic reform.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Informer TV owner Vucicevic arrested: Has the reckoning with Serbia's pro-Vucic media machine begun?
item.description: The arrest of media owner Dragan J. Vucicevic raises questions about whether Serbia is holding the people behind the country's pro-Vucic media accountable — or whether this is another political power struggle.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Duterte's ICC trial: What is at stake for the Philippines?
item.description: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte faces trial in The Hague over his deadly war on drugs. The proceedings could determine the political fortunes of a powerful dynasty. Victims' families hope to see justice.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: In Iran, child marriage risks complicated by war
item.description: War, poverty and disrupted schooling could put more girls in Iran at risk of child marriage, rights advocates have warned.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Philippines: VP Duterte says father's ICC case 'not a fair trial'
item.description: Sara Duterte has said the ICC will not give her father a fair trial and that the Hague-based court wants to "make a statement." Duterte alleges the case against her father is politically motivated.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: The tiny BSW is a party in crisis, as it is set to hand the far-right AfD power in eastern Germany
item.description: Sahra Wagenknecht's BSW party is set to disrupt German politics yet again. Espousing a mix of left-wing economic policy and populist far-right anti-migration rhetoric, it now stands to play kingmaker to the far right AfD
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Russia sports ban: Ukraine's Heraskevych hails EU pushback
item.description: As European countries challenge Russia's sporting return, Ukrainian Olympian Vladyslav Heraskevych believes the IOC is facing a "very big crisis."
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: How East Germany boosted Vietnam's coffee industry
item.description: When East Germany could no longer afford to import coffee, it introduced a substitute blend containing rye and chicory in 1977. A public outcry ensued. The solution to the problem lay 9,000 kilometers away — in Vietnam.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: AI goes from math dunce to genius
item.description: It once struggled to get simple sums right. But AI is now tackling tough mathematical problems like the Riemann hypothesis. How AI made this extraordinary leap — and why mathematicians should be "deeply worried."
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Indian workers fill Germany's labor gaps but face hurdles and risks
item.description: The number of Indians working in Germany has grown rapidly in recent years. But many continue to face challenges in the labor market. Some also fall victim to recruitment scams, leaving them vulnerable to exploitation.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: German Catholic Church abuse victims may receive higher compensation
item.description: In a landmark ruling, judges in Cologne found the Catholic Church responsible for abuse committed by clergy members. Victims could now be entitled to more compensation.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Albania's youth are protesting, no longer leaving the country
item.description: Youth protests against a rigid political system and corruption have shaken the government of Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama. They also show that fewer young people are willing to emigrate in search of a better future.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Trial of Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia begins after delay
item.description: Despite delays due to health issues, the trial of the Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia has begun. Prosecutors say the defendant used her military contacts to provide information on German defense and Ukraine.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: On farewell trip, Steinmeier calls for more investment in Africa
item.description: Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Kenya: On his last trip to Africa, outgoing German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier called on companies at home to be bolder and seize opportunities in Africa.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Freigang banned — Germany star to miss 2027 World Cup
item.description: Germany forward Laura Freigang has been suspended until October 2027 after missing three doping tests, ruling her out of next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil. Freigang has denied any intention to evade controls.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: FIFA says a cyberattack against it targeted a 'limited set of personal and business information'
item.description: World football's governing body says the cyberattack targeted personal and business information. They struck at a sensitive time for the under-fire organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: EU-Indonesia trade deal opens new markets, but challenges remain
item.description: The agreement offers new export and investment opportunities for Jakarta and Brussels. But can Indonesia turn Europe's growing interest in its markets and critical minerals into sustainable gains at home?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Joshua Kimmich critcizes Bayern bosses over Musiala health comments
item.description: Joshua Kimmich has slammed Bayern Munich's leadership over comments about Jamal Musiala's health issues. The bosses have questioned whether the player can return to previous form – and is still worth his high salary.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza coast
item.description: Authorities rescued 17 crew members but one later died in hospital after a diesel tanker capsized off the Spanish island of Ibiza. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage is now in place.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany news: Cologne court awards record damages in Catholic sex abuse case
item.description: A court has awarded the highest damages ever in Germany to a victim of sexual abuse linked to the Catholic Church. An alleged spy and suspected terrorists are also making headlines in Germany on Thursday.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany: 2 arrested, suspected of plotting synagogue attack
item.description: Federal prosecutors say they have ordered the arrest of two members of a pro-Iranian group on suspicion of planning an attack on a synagogue. They were detained in the cities of Heidelberg and Cologne.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russia-Ukraine war extends to Baltic, Mediterranean
item.description: By attacking Russian vessels around the world, Ukraine is trying to increase the pressure on Russia and also sending out signals to its Western allies. What is the impact on global maritime trade?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?
item.description: SpaceX's US Starlink satellite system has played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine, but now a Russian counterpart is under development. What could this mean for Ukraine?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Viktor Orban era
item.description: After years of frosty and hostile relations under Hungary's Kremlin-friendly former PM Viktor Orban, his successor, Peter Magyar, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy seek to reset their countries' ties.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: €561 Billion and Still Not Enough: Germany's 2027 Budget Exposes a Coalition on the Brink
item.description: The budget for 2027 has reached new highs, and pension funds, defense spending and a weak economy are increasing the pressure. At the same time, tensions are mounting within the government.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: German firms eye Africa as global trade shocks hit traditional markets
item.description: German businesses are optimistic about Africa, but Berlin's cautious approach to risk is holding them back from cashing in on the opportunities that their competitors from countries like the UAE and Turkey are seizing.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Ice hockey prospect Max Calce follows Leon Draisaitl's path, leaving Mannheim for Canada
item.description: The player widely seen as Germany's biggest ice hockey talent to come along in years is leaving the country's top professional league for Canada – changing tracks in his bid to make it to the NHL.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Climate loss and damage fund exists, but the money doesn't
item.description: Climate-vulnerable countries fought for years to create a loss and damage fund. Four years on, demand far outstrips funding, pledges are scarce, and disaster-hit nations are still waiting for support.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Germany's women's football team take stand against domestic violence
item.description: Germany's women's football team are to wear UN Women badges in games against Argentina and Peru, as domestic violence hits a record high in Germany.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: German auto workers on back foot as costs, competition bite
item.description: German auto workers profited during the industry's boom years, but are now increasingly being asked to trade past gains for future job security.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Domestic violence soars to record high in Germany
item.description: Every three days in Germany, a man kills his wife or ex-partner. Every 10 minutes, the police record a sexual offense against a woman. "A shocking finding," according to Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?
item.description: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process — often for reasons of domestic politics. DW takes a look at some cases and examines what's behind them.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: CAS reinstates Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has reinstated Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions, overturning a CAF decision that stripped them of the title. Morocco, previously declared winners, are confirmed runners-up.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Bombed factories, billion-dollar opportunity: Why German companies are staying in Ukraine
item.description: German companies remain committed to Ukraine despite million-dollar losses, an unreliable energy supply and a shortage of skilled workers. They are betting on new markets and long-term growth.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble
item.description: From Nvidia to Coreweave, AI and tech stocks have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see plenty of room to run, while others are trying to diversify — and finding it harder than expected.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: German directors' doc on stolen film wins International Emmy Award
item.description: Two German film students confronted the American who won festival prizes with their animated movie. "The Talented Mr. F," their documentary on their fight against plagiarism, is now in the spotlight.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
item.description: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Weapons, war and wavering trust: Germans want to see more restraint in foreign policy
item.description: According to a study by the Körber Foundation, a growing number of Germans now oppose providing military aid to Ukraine. The majority also believes that Germany should take a neutral position between the US and China.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: US and UK to host Women's World Cups in 2031 and 2035
item.description: FIFA has confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host the 2031 Women's World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams. The UK will stage the 2035 edition, its first World Cup since 1966.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Gukesh to defend chess crown against rising star Sindarov
item.description: As the World Chess championship gets underway, it's no coincidence that the titleholder, Gukesh Dommaraju, and his challenger, Jakhovir Sindarov, are both from Asia.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Nvidia reinstates former CEO Jensen Huang despite China espionage scandal
item.description: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring back the disgraced CEO, who resigned this month amid news of his affairs. He's suspected of having had a relationship with a Chinese intelligence asset.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate
item.description: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
item.description: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: COP deadlock prompts calls for a reset of climate diplomacy
item.description: COP31 has been branded a failure after countries couldn't reach a final agreement, divided over a reference to "fossil fuels." But was the decision to walk away from a watered-down text actually a show of strength?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: German police respond to multiple school bomb threats
item.description: Police in Germany are responding to bomb threats against a series of schools, but say that at present they don't believe them to be credible. Danish authorities are reporting a similar series of apparent hoaxes.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
item.description: For decades, Germans have known Hollywood's biggest stars through the same familiar voices. Now an AI clause in Netflix contracts is splitting the industry over whether it protects performers or exposes them.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Budget cuts threaten Germany's fight against antisemitism and racism
item.description: Numerous grassroots initiatives in Germany are facing funding cuts. Affected organizations are sounding the alarm, pointing to growing challenges posed by far-right extremism.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect
item.description: A new project and exhibition, "The Night Watch Lives," lifts the veil on the hidden world of microbes covering one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?
item.description: Germany plans to pay €10 a month into investment accounts for children to encourage long-term retirement saving. Economists say the measure may help build wealth but won't solve the country's pension funding challenge.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany news: Metalworkers go on strike as pay dispute heats up
item.description: Germany's biggest union is calling for more strikes over heated pay disputes with car makers like Mercedes and shipyards among the companies impacted. Meanwhile, a Berlin hospital fire leaves many injured.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help
item.description: Seeing someone break a rule makes people more likely to break it too, a new study has found, especially when the rule-breaker is on their side politically. Watching others behave well barely made a difference.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use
item.description: After two weeks of tough talks, the COP31 climate summit has closed without a consensus on how to quit fossil fuels or fund countries struggling to adapt to a hotter world.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029
item.description: "The Goodforces" wants to see a swing to the left in the 2029 German elections. The agency counts New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Bernie Sanders among its inspirations. Could it transform the political landscape?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Germany news: IG Metall union calls for new 24-hour strike
item.description: Germany's biggest single union, IG Metall, is calling on car and shipyard workers to strike amid a pay row. Meanwhile, Germany's president is setting off on an Africa trip. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
item.description: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
item.description: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: EU takes aim at tech giants in tax proposal
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
item.description: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad
item.description: Harassment, persecution, surveillance: Across much of the world, people of faith are facing growing pressure. A new German government report is unusually direct in criticizing China in particular.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
item.description: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading
item.description: Attacks on climate science and disinformation risk delaying key measures at COP31 in Antalya. As the UN climate talks draw to a close, how will that affect efforts to come to an agreement?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
item.description: The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future
item.description: Never before have young people around the world been so well-educated while facing so many economic challenges. Young Germans are asking: Will I be better off than my parents?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience
item.description: The US is now officially a measles contagion zone. By mid-2026, there were more infections than in all of the previous year. But the country could beat measles again, just like Brazil did two years ago.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Germany face Belgium in Nations League quarterfinals — Klopp plays down favorites tag
item.description: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is looking to "carry positive momentum forward" as his team draw neighboring Belgium in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
item.description: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
item.description: In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?
item.description: Two challengers to Gianni Infantino have registered for next year's FIFA presidential election. What do Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima stand for – and do they stand a chance against the incumbent?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, citing ongoing losses — reports
item.description: According to a letter obtained by the media, Lufthansa's executive board said the German company is losing €20 million every month. In addition to job cuts, operational cuts are also planned.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?
item.description: From record-breaking heat to devastating floods and wildfires, the warning signs are everywhere. Can rising temperatures still be brought under control?
item.dc:subject: Climate

item.title: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?
item.description: Russian President Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. But experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
item.description: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Anthropic trading tests investors' appetite for AI
item.description: Anthropic was valued at $2 trillion after shares started trading on the Nasdaq following a record $81 billion IPO. Its performance will put investor confidence in AI to the test.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend
item.description: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev is facing a new lawsuit related to a domestic abuse trial. The lawyer for his ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, told DW what the allegations are against the German player.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
item.description: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
item.description: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure
item.description: As Donald Trump seeks to tighten economic pressure on Iran, China remains its biggest oil customer and Russia a key partner. But both powers are balancing support for Tehran against broader interests with Washington.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
item.description: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
item.description: Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine
item.description: The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: How a green economy could help reverse climate change
item.description: Green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
item.description: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
item.description: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future
item.description: Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters offers hope.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?
item.description: The US says a record €3 billion financing package for Airbus may conflict with a transatlantic aircraft-subsidy truce. EU officials insist the funding complies with market-based rules.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany news: Plans for Rwanda migrant hub come under fire
item.description: Human rights groups have slammed plans by Germany and four other EU states to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. In other news, business start-ups in Germany are on track to reach the highest level since 2015.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
item.description: Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth
item.description: When just saying 'hello' takes a two-day round trip, you're a light-day, or 26 billion kilometers, from Earth. Only one human-made object has ever traveled that far — and its journey into interstellar space continues.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades
item.description: In 1962, a martini-drinking womanizer saved the world for the first time in "Dr. No." As Robert Pattinson takes on the role of 007, here's how the films evolved.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?
item.description: The Alternative for Germany party (AfD) has become a focal point for the far right. Many of its members and staff have ties to ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels
item.description: The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms
item.description: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?
item.description: In April, about 60 countries held an unprecedented meeting in Colombia to work out a plan to slowly quit oil, coal and gas. How influential is this coalition at the COP31 climate summit?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany
item.description: His life is a reflection of contemporary German history, addressed via his songs and sharp wit. At 90, he's as feisty as ever.

item.title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
item.description: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

item.title: Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany
item.description: Two weeks after the CAS ordered ice hockey's governing body to reintegrate Russia into international play, a solution remains elusive. Now Russia has threatened to take legal action against two tournament hosts.

item.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
item.description: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has said midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.

item.title: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?
item.description: The TFFF rainforest fund aims to make forest conservation more profitable than deforestation. But a lack of money may prevent it from getting off the ground.

item.title: Iranian activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi shares her story in memoir
item.description: Written and smuggled out of prison, the 2023 Nobel Prize laureate's memoir reveals the cost of defying Iran's regime and fighting for freedom.

item.title: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO over extramarital affairs. DW examines how losing its figurehead will affect the firm and the US-China AI race.

item.title: What are fossil fuels?
item.description: They are in our shampoo bottles, power our cars and heat our homes. But what actually are fossil fuels, and why do they matter?

item.title: Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds
item.description: Women who scored high on intelligence tests were seen as more hostile by their teammates and got less help, a new study finds. High-scoring men faced no such penalty. Research explains why.

item.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
item.description: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

item.title: Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?
item.description: World leaders warn that geopolitical divisions are distracting from the climate crisis as negotiations focus on clean energy and financing, while Iran calls for compensation for war-related environmental damage.

item.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
item.description: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

item.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
item.description: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

item.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
item.description: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.

item.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
item.description: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.

item.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
item.description: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

item.title: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need

item.title: Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?

item.title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health

item.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
item.description: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

item.title: Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors

item.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?

item.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
item.description: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

item.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release

item.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died

item.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
